_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: McKinsey 7S organizational-alignment analysis for teams, business units, organizations, transformations,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "Use McKinsey 7S to diagnose why this transformation is stuck after the strategy announcement."
cases.context: The agent has access to the mckinsey-7s skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is mckinsey-7s the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes mckinsey-7s as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against playing-to-win, okrs, swot-tows
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the mckinsey-7s workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore mckinsey-7s
Does not route to playing-to-win, okrs, swot-tows when the mckinsey-7s scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "Analyze buyer power, supplier power, substitutes, entrants, and rivalry in this industry."
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should mckinsey-7s be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside mckinsey-7s's ownership
Routes the work to playing-to-win or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying mckinsey-7s terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply mckinsey-7s as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if mckinsey-7s has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim mckinsey-7s should own the request
Does not use mckinsey-7s's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
